text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Coalition partners D66 and Labour PvdA agree cabinet proposal on high-speed rail HSL through the Green Heart. (p1)
- Textile firm Ten Cate is to slim-down product range. (p1)
- Telecom arm of Dutch PTT (KPN) to undego throrough restructuring but no job loss as yet. (p1)
- Consumers and small businesses will be unable to transfer money in Europe's single currency Euro until 2002. (p1)
- New-look Amsterdam bourse, combining trading in options and stocks, will only have an options trading floor, says new director George Moeller. (p1)
- Food and beverages concern BolsWessanen takes over dairy firm Ready Foods in Philadelphia, U.S. (p3)
- Royal Dutch/Shell is to restructure its western European refinery operations and cut lubricanrts production. (p4)
- Factory gate prices in the Netherlands rise sharply by 0.5 pct in October against September. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- PTT Telecom to offer electronic answering service in 1997 to fend off competition, allowed into the Dutch market. (p1)
- Automation company CMG buys Germany's software supplier Orga Team. (p2)
- Chemicals concern Hoechst Holland's restructuring of its Vlissingen plant will cost 250 of the 900 jobs. (p2)
- Rabobank chief sees higher economic growth in the Netherlands than expected by Central Planning Bureau. (p17) DE TELEGRAAF
- Endemol Entertainment is the largest creditor of bankrupt sports-only TV channel Sports 7. (p1)
- Number of occupational disabled rises again for first time in three years. (p1)
- Parliament criticises ministers in justice, foreign affairs and health depepartments for lack of coordination in dealing with France's attitude to Dutch drugs policy. (p7)
- Dutch PTT (KPN) has 93 pct of the shares of Australia's transporter TNT. (p25) TROUW
- Germany's container shipper DSR Senator Linie pulls out of Antwerp in favour of Rotterdam. (p8) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Failed introduction of new trading system Switch for the options exchange cost 35 million guilders. (p10)
- Van Hecke Catering takes over CaterRent from service group IPL, which is affiliated to chemicals concern DSM. (p11)
